capability.description: Accepted product behavior is strict, reviewable, and measurable beside the implementation.
capability.name: Living product contract

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must reject repository contract documents that violate the accepted Story and Acceptance Criterion schema.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural failures make semantic impact and synchronization untrustworthy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must compile deterministic manifests and report direct-AC and repository mapping coverage with explicit gaps.

scenarios.given: ten eligible source files and eight mapped paths
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report 80 percent coverage and name both unmapped files
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

scenarios.given: configured source roots contain no eligible files
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report that coverage is not measured instead of reporting 100 percent
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must report affected Acceptance Criteria and freshness for changed, renamed, or deleted linked paths without blocking on semantic findings.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Drift should be visible during review while the MVP remains warn-only.

scenarios.given: a linked implementation path changes without a refreshed manifest
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report the linked criterion as impacted and stale
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must render accepted Stories and Acceptance Criteria as a self-contained human-readable review page.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Maintainers outside the implementation can review the same repository-owned contract accepted by the pull request.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must store the compiled manifest as one file per capability beside a repository-level index, must delete the file of any capability the contract no longer declares, and must refuse to read a manifest whose file names disagree with the capabilities they hold.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A single generated manifest made every branch that touched any specification file conflict with every other one, even when the capabilities they changed were disjoint, and let a partial line merge produce a manifest that parses but that no compilation would emit.

scenarios.given: a compiled manifest whose capability was removed from the specification
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must delete that capability's manifest file and leave every other file in the manifest directory untouched
scenarios.when: the contract is compiled again

scenarios.given: a manifest file whose name does not match the capability it holds
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must refuse the manifest and name both the file and the capability instead of accepting the capability under the wrong identity
scenarios.when: the manifest is read

acceptance_criteria.criterion: In committed manifest mode, Tiepoint must fail the check when the committed manifest differs from the manifest the contract compiles to, unless that gate is explicitly downgraded.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A manifest merged without recompilation records evidence hashes that were never reviewed against the code they name. Comparing the committed manifest with a fresh compilation is a byte diff of a deterministic function, so nothing is being judged, which is the same reason broken links already fail. Findings that do need judgement stay warn-only.

scenarios.given: a specification file changed without the manifest being recompiled
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report the stale manifest as an error and exit non-zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: the same stale manifest and an explicit request to downgrade the gate
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report the stale manifest as a warning and exit zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: a manifest that cannot be recompiled at all
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report the compilation failure once rather than also reporting it as a stale manifest
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must require every contract link to state whether its claim was authored, inferred, or materialized, and must preserve that provenance through compiled manifests, repository synchronization, and every exact claim read.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Relation and target describe what a link claims, while provenance records how that claim entered its current authority surface. Keeping this low-cardinality origin distinct from freshness and grade lets agents interpret a claim without turning mutable review facts into contract identity.

scenarios.given: a contract link has no provenance
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must reject the link instead of guessing where its claim came from
scenarios.when: the repository contract is validated

scenarios.given: only a contract link's provenance changes
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must change the owning contract hash without creating a second link identity
scenarios.when: the contract manifest is compiled

scenarios.given: an accepted repository link was copied during planning-to-repository authority transfer
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must preserve materialized as the origin of that exact claim
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized and read

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must keep the compiled manifest independent of Git revision, identify exact manifest reads with a content-derived digest, and keep Git commit provenance separate from manifest content while supplying it explicitly for database synchronization.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A revision in the tracked repository-level index made every branch conflict in one shared generated file and became stale as soon as that generated file was committed. Content identity belongs to the reviewed manifest, while Git revision belongs to the runtime projection checkpoint and audit boundary.

scenarios.given: accepted specifications and linked artifacts whose content is unchanged across two Git revisions
scenarios.then: the repository-level manifest index must remain byte-identical and must not record either Git revision
scenarios.when: the contract is compiled at each revision

scenarios.given: the content of the reviewed manifest changes
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return a different manifest digest identifying the complete reviewed manifest that answered
scenarios.when: exact path criteria are requested

scenarios.given: a reviewed manifest and an explicit runtime Git commit
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must use that runtime commit for projection rows, checkpoint guards, sync results, and audit events without adding it to the reviewed manifest
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Compiled evidence fingerprints must identify file contents at compilation without implying semantic review, and readers must accept legacy fingerprints without losing their baseline.

scenarios.given: a version 2 manifest containing reviewed_content_hash
scenarios.then: the same baseline is available as compiled_content_hash and conflicting aliases are rejected
scenarios.when: the manifest is read by a current client

stories.benefit: intent and implementation change through the same review
stories.goal: define product behavior in a stable Story and Acceptance Criterion hierarchy
stories.title: Review accepted behavior with code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must report every acceptance criterion linked to an exact repository-relative path, must distinguish a link carried by the acceptance criterion itself from one carried only by its Story, and must return an explicit has_criteria, no_criteria, or not_found status for every requested path.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Coverage answers for the whole contract and check answers for a diff, so both describe a violation that already exists; the pre-change question is the only one that can prevent it. An empty array reads to an agent like a failed query rather than the actionable finding that an existing path has no recorded acceptance criteria.

scenarios.given: a path is linked by one acceptance criterion and by the Story that owns it
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return has_criteria with both records marked direct and story_fallback
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a path exists in the repository and no contract link targets it
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return no_criteria and state that no acceptance criteria apply instead of returning an empty result
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a requested path does not exist in the repository
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return not_found distinctly from an existing path with no criteria
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The path-criteria lookup must answer from the compiled manifest alone, so Tiepoint must serve get_path_criteria over MCP with no database connection and must return a named, actionable message when no workspace or no readable manifest is found.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Every other MCP tool fails at call time without Postgres, so an offline server boots and answers nothing; a manifest-backed lookup is what makes serving without a database worth doing, and an obscure throw would waste the one answer the caller came for.

scenarios.given: no database connection is configured
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return the applicable acceptance criteria and the content-derived digest of the manifest that answered
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested over MCP

scenarios.given: the server runs outside any Tiepoint workspace
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must name the missing workspace and the command that creates one
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested

aliases: which acceptance criteria apply to this file
stories.benefit: a contradiction with accepted behavior is prevented instead of reported afterwards
stories.goal: resolve a repository path to the acceptance criteria already recorded for it
stories.title: Learn which acceptance criteria apply to a path before editing it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact repository-relative code or test path with optional kind and selector, Tiepoint must preserve the complete locator identity, return has_context, no_criteria, or not_found explicitly, include exact-selector and file-level claims while excluding other selectors, and bound associated assets to one Acceptance-Criterion-mediated intent neighborhood.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A known symbol should retrieve the reviewed behavior that applies to that symbol without collapsing same-file claims or pretending the result is an open-ended graph traversal.

scenarios.given: one file has claims for function:first, function:second, and the whole file
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return the function:first and file-level claims with their kind, repository, canonical path, selector, framework hint, relation, provenance, and link scope while excluding function:second
scenarios.when: exact asset context is requested for function:first

scenarios.given: an existing path has no applicable claim for the requested selector
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return no_criteria distinctly from not_found for a missing path
scenarios.when: exact asset context is requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact Acceptance Criterion stable ID, Tiepoint must return its Capability and Story ancestry, lifecycle, criterion, rationale, applicability, scenarios, direct links, Story-fallback links, and directly associated code and test assets without recursive code-to-code traversal.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers need the accepted product record and its bounded contract coupling, not a semantic approximation or an inferred runtime dependency graph.

scenarios.given: an Acceptance Criterion has a direct test link and inherits a Story-level implementation link
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must preserve both assets, their direct or story_fallback scope, and the owning product context in deterministic order
scenarios.when: its exact context is requested

scenarios.given: the stable ID does not identify an accepted Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return an explicit not_found status and an actionable answer naming the unknown stable ID and reviewed manifest
scenarios.when: exact context is requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every code or test claim returned as exact intent context must keep provenance, link scope, content freshness, locator resolution, and semantic support as separate assurance dimensions, must preserve broken and uninspectable claims with honest causes or unknown states, and must report semantic support as not_assessed.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural currency and selector resolution can guide review, but neither proves the linked behavior or records that a linked test executed or passed.

scenarios.given: a current local implementation selector resolves against its reviewed content
scenarios.then: provenance, freshness, and locator resolution must be positive while semantic support remains not_assessed
scenarios.when: exact intent context is returned

scenarios.given: a local target is missing or a selector uses an unsupported language
scenarios.then: the claim must remain visible with a named broken cause or not_checked state and must not be converted into semantic failure
scenarios.when: its claim is inspected

scenarios.given: an associated target names another repository
scenarios.then: freshness and locator resolution must remain honestly unknown or not_checked
scenarios.when: its claim is inspected from this checkout

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must expose separate get_asset_intent_context and get_acceptance_criterion_context MCP tools and equivalent contract context --path and --ac CLI modes that answer from the compiled manifest without a database and preserve the same membership, statuses, repository key, and content-derived manifest digest.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Agents need primitive exact reads while maintainers need CLI and JSON parity to inspect the same reviewed contract and actionable workspace or manifest failures.

scenarios.given: no database, embeddings, network, or knowledge store is configured and the compiled manifest is readable
scenarios.then: both surfaces must return the same bounded neighborhood membership and manifest identity
scenarios.when: equivalent exact context requests are made over MCP and CLI

scenarios.given: no workspace or no readable manifest is available
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return a named actionable result that explains how to initialize or compile the workspace
scenarios.when: either MCP exact context tool is called

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Diff impact must preserve selector-qualified target identity and report resolved, unresolved, or not_checked locator state for affected links while keeping selector findings advisory and describing shared Acceptance-Criterion links only as contract coupling rather than runtime dependency or comprehensive blast radius.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Selector drift is useful review input, but conservative inspection cannot establish execution topology and must not create a new blocking gate.

scenarios.given: a changed file contains one unresolved selector claim and one selector in an unsupported source language
scenarios.then: both claims must remain distinct with unresolved and not_checked locator states and selector findings must not change the existing exit behavior
scenarios.when: diff impact is calculated

stories.benefit: implementation and review begin from bounded accepted intent with honest current assurance
stories.goal: retrieve the exact reviewed context for a known code or test locator or Acceptance Criterion
stories.title: Inspect precise accepted intent before changing an asset

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must extract deterministic symbols, owner chains where applicable, named UTF-16 and UTF-8 byte source ranges, and parser-backed source snippets from immutable JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python, Rust, and SQL snapshots while retaining syntax recovery, ambiguity, and truncation explicitly; it must also extract module references only for languages with a supported static module model.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural evidence is useful only when callers can identify the exact bytes and parser compatibility that produced it without treating a best-effort parse as semantic proof.

scenarios.given: supported source contains nested declarations, Unicode names, imports, and a recoverable syntax error
scenarios.then: facts must preserve canonical selectors, complete owners, both coordinate systems, syntax status, diagnostics, and deterministic compatibility identity
scenarios.when: the source is structurally analyzed

scenarios.given: a reviewed selector resolves uniquely against hash-current source
scenarios.then: a bounded parser-backed snippet may be returned while semantic support remains not_assessed
scenarios.when: exact intent context is read

scenarios.given: SQL declares a top-level table, view, or function with a safely representable name
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must expose its declaration selector and ranges without claiming SQL dependency edges
scenarios.when: the source is structurally analyzed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must resolve supported project-local JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, and Rust module forms in a separate conservative phase and must preserve exact, ambiguous, unresolved, external, dynamic, glob, generated, and unsupported outcomes instead of guessing a dependency.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A false edge produces a misleading blast radius, while an explicit frontier gives an agent a precise place to continue investigation.

scenarios.given: a static local import has one inventory-backed target
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must record its rule, target, configuration identity, and derived edge
scenarios.when: module resolution runs

scenarios.given: a dynamic name, glob, generated module, unsupported configuration, external package, or multiple target is encountered
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must retain a named non-resolved outcome and candidates or diagnostics without manufacturing an exact edge
scenarios.when: module resolution runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must identify topology generations from selected source and resolver inputs plus parser, resolver, schema, and fact-policy compatibility, must publish one deterministic bounded repository graph only through explicit compilation, and must publish hosted relational generations only when complete.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Readers must never observe a mixed or partial graph, generated artifact bytes must not make identity self-referential, and reviewed repository topology must remain distinct from richer hosted persistence.

scenarios.given: topology compilation is interrupted or loses a concurrent publication race
scenarios.then: readers must observe either the previous complete graph.json or the complete winning graph.json and never a partial document
scenarios.when: the artifact authority is selected

scenarios.given: files change while a working-tree generation is built
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must return workspace_changed without publishing mixed facts
scenarios.when: the consistency check retries and observes another change

scenarios.given: only generated topology bytes or unrelated authored intent change
scenarios.then: the selected-input identity must remain unchanged
scenarios.when: topology identity and artifact bytes are recomputed

scenarios.given: source roots also contain documentation, data, Tiepoint output, symbolic links, or nested repositories
scenarios.then: both must produce one selected-input identity
scenarios.when: a working tree and the commit holding the same bytes are keyed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must locate an exact path and optional selector before traversing dependencies or dependents, must default AC-aware blast radius to dependents, and must return cycle-safe deterministic paths, unresolved frontiers, generation identities, and independent depth, node, edge, and path truncation within fixed hard maxima.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Bounded topology is safe for agent use only when ambiguity and omitted work stay visible and the caller cannot bypass product limits.

scenarios.given: a dependency graph contains a cycle, diamond, ambiguous start, and unresolved reference
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must preserve all applicable start and frontier outcomes without revisiting nodes indefinitely
scenarios.when: a trace is requested

scenarios.given: a changed locator and another unrelated locator share one Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: the unrelated locator must not be traversed unless a derived code edge reaches it
scenarios.when: AC-aware blast radius runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tiepoint must expose equivalent read-only CLI and MCP artifact-backed dependency-trace and AC-aware blast-radius results, must join base and current code to their matching authored manifest roles, must label code edges as derived_code_dependency and authored joins as contract_coupling with may_be_impacted and semantic_support not_assessed, and must never infer implementation satisfaction or a code dependency from a shared Acceptance Criterion.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Derived topology can prioritize investigation and preserve deleted-side intent, but accepted YAML and its compiled manifest remain the authority for business intent and normal review remains the acceptance boundary.

scenarios.given: a local workspace has no database connection
scenarios.then: both surfaces must select the existing current repository artifact without parsing or writing and return equivalent structured membership
scenarios.when: dependency trace or AC-aware blast radius is requested

scenarios.given: a base commit removes linked code or the current manifest removes its authored claim
scenarios.then: each visited locator must join only to its matching manifest role while unclaimed locators remain visible
scenarios.when: AC-aware blast radius compares base and current

scenarios.given: hosted mode has a compatible complete topology generation but no readable authored manifest
scenarios.then: dependency trace may run while AC-aware contract joining must report contract_unavailable
scenarios.when: the tools are called

stories.benefit: code changes can be investigated with bounded structural evidence while reviewed product intent remains authoritative
stories.goal: trace conservative multi-language code relationships and their potentially affected accepted intent
stories.title: Inspect derived code topology without weakening contract authority

acceptance_criteria.criterion: In explicitly configured post_merge mode, check and grading must compile current authored definitions before review, check must still reject missing or broken evidence, grading must compare base authored YAML even when generated publication is pending, and publication freshness must remain explicit.

scenarios.given: the integration baseline has authored rules but no published manifest
scenarios.then: it must not be treated as a newly added claim
scenarios.when: an unchanged claim is graded in claims mode

scenarios.given: a current authored link targets a missing file or invalid selector
scenarios.then: the check must fail before publication
scenarios.when: the PR is checked in post_merge mode

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Explicit manifest publication must compile and validate an opted-in integration branch in a disposable worktree, commit only standard manifest output, preserve local work, avoid force pushes, retry at most three times after concurrent remote changes, and expose terminal failure without publishing an obsolete snapshot.

scenarios.given: another merge advances the remote during publication
scenarios.then: the publisher must compile the new tip before retrying
scenarios.when: the normal push is rejected

scenarios.given: the manifest already matches the fetched source
scenarios.then: no additional commit must be created
scenarios.when: publication runs again

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The generated-artifact gate must still compile and validate current authored content in post_merge mode while deferring only comparison against the published manifest and retaining topology comparison whenever topology is committed.

stories.benefit: feature branches avoid unrelated generated churn without concealing contract problems
stories.goal: automate fingerprint publication while reviewing behavior before merge
stories.title: Maintain generated manifests after integration

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When topology_mode is absent or cached, explicit compilation of the workspace or of an immutable Git revision must publish its graph only to an ignored cache entry named by that snapshot's selected-input digest, and workspace and revision readers must select only the entry for the exact snapshot they inspect, without parsing or writing, reporting missing, stale, incompatible, invalid, unsafe, or oversized entries as named failures that include the digest.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A committed graph carries digests of the whole selected tree, so any two concurrent changes to selected inputs conflict on it and every textual resolution is stale. Keying the graph by the digest readers already compute keeps freshness exact while removing the file from pull requests.

scenarios.given: two branches change independent source files from one base
scenarios.then: the merge must not conflict on topology and both orders must yield one byte-identical graph that includes dependencies created only by the combination
scenarios.when: they merge in either order and the merged tree is compiled

scenarios.given: the workspace was edited after its last compile
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report topology_missing for the new digest rather than serve the earlier graph
scenarios.when: validate, trace, or blast radius reads topology

scenarios.given: a blast-radius base commit has not been compiled
scenarios.then: Tiepoint must report topology_missing_at_revision naming the revision compile to run
scenarios.when: the base comparison runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An explicit committed topology_mode must keep the reviewed graph.json lifecycle without consulting the cache, and in cached mode a legacy committed graph may answer only while it is current for the exact snapshot, must never be updated by compilation, and must be removable by an untrack command that seeds the cache from a current legacy graph, stages only its removal and the topology ignore rule, resolves a modify/delete conflict on that file, and never commits or pushes.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Repositories that already commit topology must keep working on upgrade, and the heal must not touch history or unrelated paths.

scenarios.given: a repository upgrades while its committed graph is current
scenarios.then: the legacy graph must answer and a notice must point to untrack
scenarios.when: topology is read before any recompilation

scenarios.given: a branch still modifies graph.json after main removed it
scenarios.then: the conflict must resolve by removing the derived file
scenarios.when: the merge conflicts and untrack runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: In cached topology mode the generated-artifact gate must still compile, validate, and smoke-test topology through its cached reader while omitting only the reviewed-graph byte comparison, and must keep manifest comparison enforced.

stories.benefit: independent pull requests stop conflicting on generated topology while stale or forged graphs stay detectable
stories.goal: keep derived topology current for every inspected snapshot without committing it in feature pull requests
stories.title: Compile topology per snapshot instead of committing it
